title: Machine-Checked Exact-Rational Sign-Vector Flags, Quasipolyhedral Non-Attainment, Frame Slices, and Acyclic Chamber DAG Certificates for Hyperplane Arrangements
abstract: Brennan Dury (arXiv:2611.32976, November 24, 2026) constructed directed acyclic graphs on the chambers of locally finite affine hyperplane arrangements driven by a nonconstant affine objective omega: at every bounded chamber c, a flag of faces based at its optimal face F of codimension r generates 2^r - 1 outgoing target chambers via an exact sign-flip formula; both an inner-product (Euclidean) and a covector-frame (Frame) strategy induce acyclic chamber digraphs in which every sufficiently long walk escapes to a strictly larger optimal value, and every affine objective bounded above on a closed face attains its supremum on a closed face. We present a machine-checked, zero-floating-point formalization and exact-Q certificate auditor for the combinatorial, geometric, and LP-duality core of this construction. First, an 18-theorem zero-dependency Lean 4 kernel (HyperplaneTraversal.lean, Lean 4.35.0; 0 sorry, 0 warnings, 0 Classical.choice, 5 zero-axiom theorems) formalizes Proposition 1 sign-closure poset axioms, Theorem 2's 2^r - 1 target fanout, identity at 1^r, mutual distinctness, and base containment, Section 2 Figure 2's quasipolyhedral non-attainment counterexample (l_n(x) = 2^{-(n+1)}(x-n-2) hitting {0} x [-1,0] for all n >= 0), and the scalar algebraic projections of Lemma 4, Lemma 15, Lemma 17, Proposition 3, and Theorem 3. Second, ARRANGEMENT-TRAVERSAL-CERT-1.0 audits four exact-Q modes—including exact codimension ranks, full-rank tangent cones, strict-complementarity KKT witnesses certifying x* in relint(F(c)), and exact Theorem 2 2^r - 1 target closures—across 16 canonical certificates (0.110-1.003 ms) and rejects 66/66 live adversarial forgeries.
